intro: Belize’s tropical climate allows year-round planting with irrigation. Time new trees with rainfall for the strongest start.

bestWindows.title: Primary planting window
bestWindows.detail: Just before and into the rainy season. Roots establish quickly with natural rainfall.

bestWindows.title: Secondary window
bestWindows.detail: After peak rains, while soils are still moist. Excellent for citrus and avocado.

months.advice: Plant with irrigation. Ideal for citrus, coconut, and container trees. Mulch heavily.
Continue irrigated plantings. Prune established mangoes after harvest. Watch for mites in dry heat.
Hottest stretch begins. Water young trees twice weekly. Good month to order for May planting.
Prepare holes and compost. Avocado ‘April’ and early mangoes often fruit now. Hold off on bare-root moves.
Best month to plant most fruit trees. Rains arrive. Grafted mango, avocado, and citrus take off.
Prime planting. Passion fruit, guava, soursop, and lychee establish well. Stake in windy sites.
Still excellent for planting. Watch drainage in heavy clay. Apply compost around drip line.
Plant on mounds if flooding is a risk. Good for banana relatives, coconut, and breadfruit.
Peak rains. Focus on weeding and disease watch. Hold delicate air-layers until soils firm.
Late rainy-season planting still works with raised beds. Begin dry-season irrigation plans.
Second-best planting window. Cooler nights help citrus, peach, and pomegranate.
Plant with a watering plan. Holiday citrus makes a beautiful gift tree. Mulch and protect from wind.
